Watch: BBC follows operation to rescue shark stranded in South Korean canalByJake Kwon, Reporting fromBusan, and Koh EwePublished22 October 2026, 05:12 BSTUpdated 7 minutes ago
A famed dusky shark in South Korea is still lingering near a canal that it was guided out of on Wednesday.
The shark, nicknamed Bukangi, became an unlikely sensation after it was spotted swimming in a canal in the south-eastern port city of Busan last month. For weeks, rescuers tried in vain to get it back to the open sea using large nets.
On Thursday, authorities said they had reinforced barriers to prevent Bukangi from returning. But it has yet to swim out into the open sea, and has been circling back repeatedly to the mouth of the waterway.
Its rescue prompted mixed reactions in Busan, where some said the shark should stay while others felt it was better for it to go.
In a livestreamed operation on Wednesday, rescue workers took more than eight hours to delicately guide the three-metre-long (10ft) shark with a net towards open water in a harbour.
Hundreds of adoring fans gathered at the park overlooking the canal, cheering and waving goodbye to the shark.
But then, on Thursday morning, Bukangi reportedly swam back into the canal after breaking through a barrier installed by authorities.
For some time, Bukangi was trapped in a tight space between two layers of nets in the canal.
Rescuers freed it by removing the outer layer, and have since fortified the remaining layer of nets to prevent it from going back in.
Since then, authorities said, Bukangi has been swimming further out but keeps circling back.
A government official told the BBC on Thursday afternoon that rescuers had concluded their operations to free the shark.

item.description:
Image source, ReutersImage caption,
Dammam is the largest city in Saudi Arabia's oil-rich Eastern ProvinceByDavid GrittenPublished1 hour ago
Two people were killed and eight others injured in an attack on an airport in Dammam, eastern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday evening, the kingdom's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) says.
Those killed at King Fahd International Airport were a Saudi citizen and an Indian resident, while the injured were Saudi, Indian, Yemeni, Bangladeshi and Nepalese nationals.
The GACA did not say what type of attack occurred, but Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement has repeatedly targeted the kingdom's airports with drones and missiles.
On Wednesday morning, two people were killed by debris from a drone that was intercepted over Eastern Province, where Dammam is located, the Saudi energy ministry said.
The ministry said the drone was intercepted as it attempted to target a processing facility owned by Saudi Arabia's state oil company Aramco in the Shaybeh oil field, where a contractor's vehicle was set ablaze.
It identified the dead as residents from the Philippines and Nepal.
Another four drones were also intercepted on Wednesday night, according to the Saudi-led coalition that is supporting the Yemeni government in its war against the Houthis.
There was no immediate comment from the Houthis, but they have previously said they are attacking Saudi airports, energy facilities and military bases in retaliation for deadly Saudi air strikes on the territory they control in western Yemen.

item.title: [ABC News World] Women are protesting around Poland for free access to legal abortions
item.description:
Women are protesting around Poland for free access to legal abortions
Women are protesting in Poland for access to free and legal abortion servicesByCLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated PressOctober 22, 2026, 2:36 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
WARSAW, Poland -- Women plan street demonstrations in more than 20 Polish cities and towns Thursday to protest the lack of access to free and legal abortion.
They're accusing Prime Minister Donald Tusk's liberal government of failing to fulfill its promise to relax Poland's strict abortion laws, and protesting even though the parliament passed two bills on Tuesday aimed at easing abortion rules. The measures are likely to be vetoed by the conservative president, Karol Nawrocki.
Passing the draft laws now, a year before the next parliamentary election, is a case of “token gestures” rather than a genuine effort to reform abortion law, said Zofia Marcinek of the Abortion Dream Team, a reproductive rights activist group in Warsaw.
She said the liberal government knew the draft laws stand no chance of withstanding Nawrocki's veto, and has merely tried to create the impression of taking action because it needs women's support to win elections next year.
Since 1993, legal abortions have been allowed in Catholic Poland only in cases of severe fetal abnormality, risk to the mother’s life and health, or the pregnancy being a result of rape or incest.
Polish women have been pushing for the legalization of abortion ever since, including in a nationwide wave of demonstrations of women wearing black called “Black Protest,” which began in 2016.
Rather than being liberalized, Poland’s abortion laws were tightened further, banning abortions of fetuses with congenital defects in 2020 under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government.
Despite the laws, abortions remain common in Poland, an overwhelming majority of which are carried out by women at home using pills obtained from outside the country. Wo...

item.title: [BBC World] How Arab parties could hold critical balance of power in Israeli election
item.description:
Image caption,
Students in Nazareth are handing out leaflets encouraging Arab Israelis to vote in next week's electionByYolande KnellMiddle East correspondent, Reporting fromNazarethPublished4 hours ago
At rush hour in Nazareth, the largest Arab-majority city in Israel, students are handing out leaflets by the roadside urging motorists to vote in next week's closely fought, general election. Polls indicate that Arab parties could be left holding a critical balance of power.
Disaffection has often driven down past turnout among Arab Israelis - who account for about a fifth of the population and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel. But this election, there is a strong push to get rid of the most right-wing governing coalition in the country's history - an alliance between veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties.
"I see it as our duty to bring down this extremist government. They treat us as second-class," says Arkan Badran, 23, who is with the students giving out flyers. "I call on all young men and women to vote for Arab lists, which represent us, because this is our future."
Image caption,
All but one of the leading Jewish parties have ruled out forming a coalition government with Arab parties
Most opinion polls indicate that neither Netanyahu and his partners nor the main "Change Bloc", led by centre-right former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has a clear path to a parliamentary majority.
If they are right, after the election anti-Netanyahu parties wanting to form a governing coalition would either have to go back on pledges not to work with the prime minister or make a deal with Arab-majority lists.
A major sticking point is that Eisenkot has so far ruled out forming a government with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values.

item.title: [CBS News World] Elon Musk's Starlink and Starshield, and what they mean to Ukraine
item.description:
Over the past week, Ukraine has received a stark reminder of its growing dependence on uninterrupted access to Elon Musk's Starlink and Starshield networks in its drone-heavy war against Russia, now in its fifth year.
Ukraine has a fraction of Russia's resources, but its aggressive development of drone warfare on defensive and offensive fronts has helped it endure an onslaught from its much bigger adversary, which invaded Ukraine in early 2022. That was true until last week, when Ukraine reported a throttling of the Starshield network that was causing its drones to stop midflight and fall out of the sky.
The two SpaceX networks operate on a constellation of thousands of low-Earth satellites — Starlink is the commercial version, while Starshield is a military product licensed to the U.S. government and its partners, among them Ukraine.
Kyiv's reliance on drones has made Starlink and Starshield nearly indispensable to its arsenal. When Ukraine experienced a disruption to those networks, it lost the shield of interceptors and drones that offered some protection against Russian drone and missile strikes.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy believes Musk throttled Starshield at the request of U.S. officials, though the world's richest man has denied any role and said it's the U.S. government that controls the military-grade network. President Trump has also denied he's responsible for slowing the network. However, CBS News reported Tuesday that Musk was behind the disruption, though a number of questions remain unanswered.
There has also been conflicting information about whether full access to the networks has been restored. As of Wednesday afternoon, Starlink remained throttled, Zelenskyy's office confirmed.

item.title: [BBC China] No order, no seat: Starbucks China rolls out new store policy
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
"Purchase to sit" signs are popping up in Starbucks stores around ChinaByKoh EwePublished6 hours ago
Taking a seat at a Starbucks in China? Just make sure you're also ordering something there.
A new policy by Starbucks China takes effect across all its 8,000 stores on Thursday, making it mandatory for people to purchase items if they want to sit in its cafes.
Starbucks China said the move was part of efforts to improve the "in-store experience" for customers. The company is facing stiff competition from homegrown brands such as Luckin Coffee.
Starbucks stores around the world have also been wrestling with non-paying seat-hoggers and other undesirable behaviour from customers.
In South Korea, Starbucks has told customers to stop bringing "bulky items" into their stores, after some patrons reportedly hogged seats with printers and desktop computers in tow.
In North America, Starbucks reversed its open-door policy which for years allowed people to use their seats and toilets without buying anything, saying that it wanted to "prioritise" paying customers.
Starbucks China is now following suit.
Ahead of the official announcement on Wednesday, reports of the new seating policy at China's Starbucks stores had been circulating this week - along with social media videos of what appear to be "purchase to sit" signs in Starbucks stores.
Many on Chinese social media welcomed the new policy.
"Finally, there won't be peak periods where people are just sitting there not ordering anything, drinking Luckin coffee, playing games and yelling on the phone," reads one of the top-liked comment on Weibo. "Every time I walk around, there's nowhere to sit,"
"There's nothing wrong with it. I'd feel awkward sitting there if I didn't make a purchase. I'd rather leave the seats for those who made purchases and need the seats," another Weibo user commented.

item.title: [CBS News World] Son of Stephen Hubbard, American freed from Russian jail, speaks out
item.description:
Washington — Fr. Joseph Coleman feared he would never again see his father, Stephen Hubbard, when they had a brief phone conversation last year while Hubbard was in a Russian prison.
"He was expressing a very extreme tiredness with life, the life that he was experiencing at that time. I don't want to say suicidal thoughts, but the conversation hinted it leaned in that direction," Coleman, a Greek Orthodox priest, told CBS News on Wednesday in his first television interview since his father's release.
Hubbard's release was announced earlier Wednesday during a meeting between U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Hubbard, a U.S. citizen, was imprisoned in Russia for more than four years after being accused of fighting for Ukraine. The U.S. government had deemed Hubbard wrongfully detained.
President Trump said Putin had agreed to release Hubbard at his request, with "no 'swap' necessary," though he also said that his decision to waive new sanctions against Russia played a role in Hubbard's release.
In a one-minute phone call with his father before Hubbard took off from St. Petersburg, Coleman said he sounded better than he had during their last conversation in May 2025. Witkoff was also present, leaving little opportunity for a private exchange.
"I want to embrace him as a son embraces his father. I want to personally assess his health to make sure he's well," Coleman said. He said he would also give his dad space to adjust to freedom and expected to see Hubbard later that evening.
Coleman, who lives in Cyprus, did not grow up in the same home as Hubbard, who was divorced from Coleman's mother. He said the family had lost track of Hubbard entirely for roughly three years after his detention.
Martin De Luca, Hubbard's U.S.-based attorney, told CBS News that when his legal team took on the case in February 2025, neither the family nor the U.S. Embassy knew precisely where Hubbard was being held.

item.title: [Guardian World] Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted
item.description:
A woman stands in a shared room at a residential care facility for pregnant mothers in Gabu, Guinea Bissau, on 22 May 2012. Photograph: Rebecca Blackwell/AP
View image in fullscreen
A woman stands in a shared room at a residential care facility for pregnant mothers in Gabu, Guinea Bissau, on 22 May 2012. Photograph: Rebecca Blackwell/AP
Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted
Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’
The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.
It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”
The minister of health in Guinea-Bissau, Quinhin Nantote, previously denied that the project would move forward. “This is not even remotely true,” Nantote told the Guardian in Portuguese last week.
The study was to be funded with $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), along with another $1.6m from private partners like the Bill Ackman-backed Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation.
“The solution is clear here: take the money and vaccinate as many kids as you can,” said Paul Offit, a vaccines expert at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, who sharply criticized the proposed study as unethical.
The government of Guinea-Bissau now has control over the researchers’ vaccines, which they apprehended when they searched the offices of the Bandim Health Project on Monday.
It was vital to support Guinea-Bissau in rolling the immunizations out to all newborns as soon as possible, Offit said. Guinea-Bissau currently plans to offer the universal birth dose in 2028.

item.title: [Guardian China] Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes
item.description:
Huang Yi-hao was left with a bruised pelvis after the men rammed him with a car while he was riding his scooter. Photograph: Huang Yi-hao/Facebook
View image in fullscreen
Huang Yi-hao was left with a bruised pelvis after the men rammed him with a car while he was riding his scooter. Photograph: Huang Yi-hao/Facebook
Taiwan charges five men over plot to run over comedian for his Xi Jinping jokes
Person named ‘K’ from China paid five defendants to injure Huang Yi-hao, New Taipei prosecutors say
Taiwanese prosecutors have charged five men over a plot to ram a car into a comedian who made fun of the Chinese Communist party and Xi Jinping.
Taiwan has repeatedly accused China of transnational repression to silence critics on the self-governed island, which Beijing claims as its territory and has vowed to take by force if necessary.
In one performance, Huang Yi-hao insulted the Chinese leader’s appearance, compared him to Winnie-the-Pooh and tore into his political record.
Prosecutors in New Taipei said on Wednesday that an individual from mainland China who was identified as “K” had paid the five defendants to injure Huang badly enough to require hospitalisation.
The prosecutors said: “This case involves a serious incident in which the Chinese Communist party is suspected of using cross-border suppression tactics to direct lawless elements in our country to suppress dissenting political voices through extreme violence.”
China’s Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to requests for comment.
A GPS tracker was allegedly put on Huang’s scooter months before the attack to identify his daily routines, Taiwan’s Central News Agency said. On 11 September, two defendants drove into Huang’s bike as he rode home, but stopped after hearing Huang scream, prosecutors said.
The comedian was left with a bruised pelvis and the suspects then allegedly pretended to help with an insurance claim in order to send a photo of Huang’s medical certificate to K.

item.title: [Guardian World] Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say
item.description:
The Krome detention center in west Miami, Florida, on the Fourth of July in 2025. Photograph: Pedro Portal/Miami Herald via Getty Images
View image in fullscreen
The Krome detention center in west Miami, Florida, on the Fourth of July in 2025. Photograph: Pedro Portal/Miami Herald via Getty Images
Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say
Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail
Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms
Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.
Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities in south Florida.
The group said multiple sick detainees with varying conditions had been targeted for imminent deportation, and learned about the operation only in the last few days.
“I received a call from several detainees letting me know that men were being pulled in to interviews with deportation agents, where they were being informed that because of their medical conditions, Mexico would not be accepting their entry, and they will be sent to Africa,” Arianne Betancourt, the group’s immigrant rights organizer, said at a Tuesday night press conference.
“We know that once they are deported and sent to these third countries, they are not receiving medical care in detention. They have difficulties getting medicine.”

item.title: [ABC News World] Australian politician who was hit by car has lost both legs
item.description:
Australian politician who was hit by car has lost both legs
Australian federal lawmaker Helen Haines had had both legs amputated after she was rammed repeatedly by a driver on Monday outside her electorate office, her husband saysByROD MCGUIRK Associated Press and CHARLOTTE GRAHAM-MCLAY Associated PressOctober 21, 2026, 3:28 AM
MELBOURNE, Australia -- Doctors have amputated both of Australian federal lawmaker Helen Haines ' legs as she remains in critical condition after being repeatedly hit by a car in an apparent act of political violence, her husband said Wednesday.
The 65-year-old independent politician is receiving treatment in a Melbourne hospital where she was flown by helicopter.
Phil Haines, her husband, gave the family’s first public comments on her condition since she was hit by a Toyota Land Cruiser SUV in her hometown of Wangaratta on Monday, speaking hours after a man accused of running her over made an initial appearance in court.
Haines' husband said her left leg was amputated on Monday and her right leg was amputated on Wednesday after doctors abandoned hope of saving it.
“The good news in all this is that Helen is alive and she’s stable. That is the most important thing for our family,” the husband told reporters in Melbourne.
“We are grateful and thankful that at this stage, both her heart and her mind are in good shape,” he said.
He added that their 40th wedding anniversary will be in November.
Earlier Wednesday, Brendan Nugent, a 43-year-old man from nearby Tarrawingee, appeared in the Wangaratta Magistrates’ Court charged with intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury and causing harm to a federal official.
Nugent didn’t apply for bail or enter a plea. He will remain in custody until his next court appearance in February. Police have yet to determine a motive.

UK government approves natural gas project despite environmental concerns
The U.K. government has approved a natural gas project off the coast of Scotland over the objections of environmental groups, saying it would improve energy security as the country transitions to renewable sources of energyByThe Associated PressOctober 21, 2026, 2:59 AM
LONDON -- The U.K. government approved a natural gas project off the coast of Scotland over the objections of environmental groups on Wednesday, saying it would improve energy security as the country transitions to renewable sources of energy.
While the Jackdaw field east of Aberdeen was originally approved in 2022, it stalled after a Scottish court ruled the government had failed to consider the environmental impact of burning gas produced by the project.
After further review, Energy Minister Miatta Fahnbulleh approved the project on Wednesday.

Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda
Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.
The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

item.title: [Guardian China] US bans use of China’s DeepSeek AI tools by government agencies
item.description:
The smartphone app DeepSeek. Photograph: Andy Wong/AP
View image in fullscreen
The smartphone app DeepSeek. Photograph: Andy Wong/AP
US bans use of China’s DeepSeek AI tools by government agencies
Use of tools ‘may result in the transfer of sensitive data’ to China, defense department says
The US government on Monday ordered its agencies to stop using artificial intelligence (AI) tools from the Chinese startup DeepSeek, as the countries race for dominance in the fast-moving sector.
A notice from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced the ban on products developed by DeepSeek – and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties – saying they must be removed from IT devices.
The DHS can issue direction to civilian agencies but not the military or intelligence services. The US defense department did not respond to an AFP request for comment.
“DeepSeek’s models present multiple threat vectors,” said a document attached to Monday’s notice.
Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to [China] if used by US government employees or vendors”, the department warned.
Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said.
DeepSeek has been contacted for comment.
One of China’s top AI labs, DeepSeek shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance.
The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April, and earlier in October updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4.
The US has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals.
Despite their fierce competition in the field, when their leaders Xi Jinping and Donald Trump met at the White House in September, China and the US agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents.

item.description:
‘Trumpian America is raising doubts about whether it will help deter aggression or even honour its Nato commitments.’ Photograph: José Luis Magaña/AP
View image in fullscreen
‘Trumpian America is raising doubts about whether it will help deter aggression or even honour its Nato commitments.’ Photograph: José Luis Magaña/AP
The Guardian view on Trump and Putin: Ukraine’s future is not theirs to bargain away Editorial
Russia wants America and China to decide Ukraine’s future without Kyiv. Europe must challenge this dangerous return to diplomacy of the strong for the strong
Does Vladimir Putin know exactly how to play Donald Trump? The history of chummy phone calls, high-profile meetings and attempts to bring Russia in from the cold certainly suggests that Moscow’s thuggish ruler has a hold on this American president. If Mr Trump agrees to negotiate Ukraine’s future with Mr Putin and China’s Xi Jinping without Ukraine at the table, he will have handed the Russian leader a victory before talks begin. The message will be that strongmen are ruling the world and determining the fate of weaker nations.
Ukraine has the right to determine its future. That right cannot be waved away by a self-serving Russian proposal, however much it indulges Mr Trump’s belief that world affairs should be settled by powerful men. The scales are falling from European eyes. Trumpian America is raising doubts about whether it will help deter aggression or even honour its Nato commitments. If Washington now rewards Moscow and pressures Ukraine to accept a raw deal, it would be a betrayal. European governments would wonder where America might be in the future when their own security is threatened.

item.title: [BBC China] China tells Israel to stop 'forced establishment' of West Bank settlements
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
China has been positioning itself as a mediator for conflicts in the Middle EastByKoh EwePublished16 October 2026
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has told Israel to stop its "forced establishment" of settlements in the West Bank and reverse its actions, his office said.
The "Palestinian question" is "the greatest historical injustice of this century", Wang told Israeli President Isaac Herzog in a face-to-face meeting on the sidelines of a conference in Azerbaijan on Thursday.
Beijing has been a long-standing supporter of the Palestinian cause and has maintained that a "two-state solution" is the "correct direction".
It has also been positioning itself as a mediator for conflicts in the Middle East.
In 2023 Beijing brokered a deal to restore diplomatic ties between Iran and Saudi Arabia after years of hostility. Earlier this year, it was part of efforts, along with Pakistan, to propose a ceasefire in the US-Israel war against Iran.
Beijing's efforts to tackle the war in Gaza have focused on Palestinian unity.
In 2024 Beijing got rival Palestinian factions to agree to form an interim "national reconciliation government" for the occupied West Bank and Gaza after the war with Israel, although it was never implemented.
Now, Wang says the "immediate priority" is to fully open access to Gaza and stop the continued spread of a "humanitarian catastrophe".
China is willing to work with the international community to get the parties to return to dialogue and "seek a political solution to the conflict", he said.
In a post on X, Herzog said he was "pleased" to meet Wang and their talk "focused on the relations between our countries and the situation in the Middle East".
"I emphasised Israel's desire for peace in the region, alongside the strategic threats to our security, first and foremost from Iran and its terror proxies," he wrote.

item.title: [BBC China] North Korea and China open new bridge after 12-year delay
item.description:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption,
The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North KoreaByKoh Ewe and Julianna KhanPublished15 October 2026
A long-delayed road bridge linking China and North Korea has opened, Chinese state media report, as trade ties improve between the neighbours.
China is North Korea's largest trading partner and a lifeline against heavy international sanctions over Pyongyang's nuclear weapons programme.
The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North Korea, and is set to become the main land route for trade between them.
Its launch, initially slated for 2014, had been indefinitely postponed after North Korea halted construction of its roads and customs facilities, as relations with Beijing turned frosty.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang, in a video address on Thursday, said the bridge was a "new landmark symbolising the traditional friendship between China and North Korea", and that the two countries were "opening a new chapter" in bilateral ties.
The New Yalu River Bridge is an alternative to the decades-old Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which was built between 1937 and 1943 during Imperial Japan's occupation of the region.
The new bridge is an "important facility for connectivity" between the two countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Wednesday, adding that the route would "further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges".
Last year, bilateral trade reached $2.7bn, marking a recovery to pre-pandemic levels, mostly fuelled by Chinese exports to North Korea.
A sharp and sudden increase in trade across the border is "unlikely" as the UN sanctions on North Korea remain in effect, Kang Jun-young, a professor of Chinese studies at the Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, tells the BBC.
